page: Microsoft Azure E96bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EBDSv5 server family, designed for high-performance block storage and memory-intensive workloads. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled 3686 GB local SSD storage array.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 93257.53 and a Passmark CPU score of 76619.46. Memory performance is highly competitive, registering a strong read-only small block cached bandwidth of 5005.81 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 139.89 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations are exceptionally efficient, achieving a top-tier Passmark encryption score of 86971.74. However, single-core performance remains moderate, as reflected by average scores in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

The instance offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise-scale database operations and memory-bound applications, though the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy AI workloads. This is highlighted by a weak text generation speed of 2.73 tokens/sec during large 70B LLM inference benchmarks. The server is highly suited for relational databases, large-scale Redis deployments, software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E96bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EBDSv5 family, featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 3686 GB local SSD. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers strong multi-core performance, high memory bandwidth, and top-tier cryptographic execution. While single-core benchmarks and large LLM inference speeds represent notable performance tradeoffs, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and block storage capabilities make it highly cost-efficient for resource-dense workloads. It is best suited for enterprise databases, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
